metadata.case_name: WONG SHUN CHI v. THAI EAST TEXTILE CO. LTD. AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: chamber maid at the Miramar Hotel

injuries.description: fracture of both tibiae and fibulae bones of the lower leg
source: The first report revealed that the plaintiff suffered a fracture of both tibiae and fibulae bones of the lower leg.
After three weeks the fracture of the right tibiae was secured by a bone plate and screws and of the tibiae by insertion of an intramedullary nail.

injuries.description: arterial damage to the foot resulting in numbness on walking
source: However, the report of May 1984 reveals that the numbness in the left foot following five to ten minutes of walking still persisted.

Dr. Wedderburn said that this was because of arterial damage. Consequently, upon the muscles of the foot being used for walking there was insufficient blood to supply the oxygen required by the muscles.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of unspecified blood vessel at ankle or foot level

manifestations.description: numbness in her left foot after walking for five to ten minutes
walked with great difficulty for up to a month after the operation

treatments_received: fixation of right tibia with a bone plate and screws
removal of metal plates (operation in February 1983)
use of a stick for 1 month
hospitalisation until discharged at the end of January

losses.description: Pain suffering and loss of amenities were agreed at $50,000.
Required the use of crutches for 6 months and a stick for one month; had a very mild limp and difficulty walking.
She was no longer capable of working as a maid in an hotel.
